patients.summary: Young woman with longstanding epilepsy (irregular levetiracetam), mild persistent asthma and secondary amenorrhea who joins in 2019, develops SLE with arthropathy in 2021, then class IV lupus nephritis after stopping medicines for cost, two episodes of status epilepticus, a medically managed type B aortic dissection with a bicuspid valve and dilated root, and a traumatic subdural hematoma with herniation needing craniotomy after a car crash.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is looking for a new primary care doctor; says her old office kept moving her to whoever was free and she never saw the same person twice. Works retail, schedule changes week to week, asked whether texting the office is really an option. Explained membership and that labs, specialists and pharmacy still go through her own coverage or self-pay. She is currently uninsured and understands those costs are separate. New patient visit booked for 10/8 at 9:00. Release signed for prior office and her neurologist's office; records request sent.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
25 y/o woman establishing care. Wants one doctor who knows her.

Seizures: has had epilepsy for years, on levetiracetam 500 mg BID. Honest that she misses doses, mostly the evening one when she closes at the store. Last seen by a neurologist a while back; old office refilled it since. No seizure she can recall in recent months but not certain.
Asthma: fluticasone 44, two puffs twice a day, plus albuterol when wheezy. Uses rescue inhaler a couple of times a month, more with colds. No ED visits for asthma.
Periods: none for a long time; was looked at by her last office for missed periods. Never been pregnant.

Allergy: sulfa antibiotics, blotchy rash.
PSH: none.
FH: mother has lupus. Mom's sister has rheumatoid arthritis. Father on BP medicine. Paternal grandfather had seizures.
SH: married, lives with husband. Retail sales associate. Never smoked. A drink or so once or twice a month. No drugs.

Exam: well appearing, petite. Vitals as recorded. HEENT unremarkable. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, nontender. Joints without swelling. Skin clear. Neuro grossly nonfocal, gait normal.

A/P
1. Epilepsy - continue levetiracetam 500 BID; talked through phone alarms and a weekly pill box. Will get her neurology records.
2. Asthma, mild persistent - controlled on low-dose inhaled steroid. Refills sent.
3. Secondary amenorrhea - records from prior office pending; urine hCG negative today.
4. Health maintenance - flu and Tdap given today. HIV and hep C screening, CBC, CMP drawn. Pap was done last year per her, will confirm on records.
RTC 4 months or sooner. Text or call anytime.

documents.title: After Visit Summary
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Keep taking levetiracetam 500 mg morning and evening. Set two phone alarms. Keep your fluticasone twice daily and rinse after. We will call with your blood test results. Next visit in about 4 months.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Ms. Chapman - your blood count, kidney and liver tests are normal. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. Good to meet you.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office

documents.body: Received 34 pages from prior primary care practice. Problem list: epilepsy, mild persistent asthma, amenorrhea. Medications: levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily, fluticasone 44 mcg inhaler 2 puffs twice daily, albuterol as needed. Allergy: sulfa (rash). Cervical cytology 2018: negative for intraepithelial lesion. Prior neurology letter (several years old): generalized epilepsy, on levetiracetam, adherence discussed. Amenorrhea visit note: urine pregnancy test negative, follow-up advised. Scanned to chart.

orders.reason: inflammatory arthritis with photosensitive malar rash; mother with lupus

documents.title: Office Visit - joint pain, rash
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted Monday about sore knees and wrists, seen today.

S: About five weeks of aching and swelling in both knees and both wrists. Stiff and worst first thing in the morning, loosens up as the day goes on, which makes opening the store hard. More tired than usual. Red rash across her cheeks and nose that flares when she is outside in the sun. No fevers. No chest pain like last time. Mom has lupus and she is worried.

O: Both wrists and both knees puffy and tender, not hot, not red. Full but painful ROM. Erythematous rash over the malar areas and bridge of nose, sparing the nasolabial folds. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No oral ulcers seen.

A/P: symmetric inflammatory arthritis plus photosensitive malar rash, prior pleurisy, strong family history - concerning for SLE. Referred to rheumatology, asked them to see her soon and do the serologic workup there since she is self-pay and they will need their own panel anyway. Sun protection. Flu shot given. Will call her when appointment set.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Rheumatology office called back: first new-patient opening 12/20, put on cancellation list. Pt informed. Gave her the number for the hospital financial counselor for the self-pay labs; she will call.

documents.title: Rheumatology Consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside Rheumatology Clinic - New Patient Consultation
Date of service: 12/20/2021
Referred by: primary care
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics (rash)

Reason: polyarthralgia with swelling, facial rash.

History: 27-year-old woman with three months of pain and swelling of the knees and wrists. Morning predominance with improvement as the day goes on. Newer fatigue. Facial rash brought out by sun. Background of mild asthma and a pleurisy episode roughly two years back. Epilepsy on levetiracetam, adherence imperfect. Amenorrhea. Mother with SLE; maternal aunt with RA.

Current medicines: levetiracetam 500 mg bid, fluticasone inhaler, albuterol prn.

Exam: Bilateral knee and wrist effusions/synovial swelling with tenderness; no significant warmth or erythema. Malar erythema across both cheeks and the nasal bridge. No alopecia. Heart and lungs unremarkable.

Data: Hgb 11.2, WBC 3.8, platelets 120 K. ESR 50. ANA positive 1:640. Anti-dsDNA positive. Anti-Smith positive. C3 and C4 both low.

Impression: Systemic lupus erythematosus with inflammatory arthropathy, malar rash, cytopenias and hypocomplementemia.

Plan:
- Prednisone 20 mg daily.
- Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily.
- Strict sun protection.
- Labs with PCP in about 3 months including urinalysis and creatinine.
- Return here in 4 months.
Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Call re lupus diagnosis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called her after reading the rheumatology letter. She has started prednisone 20 and hydroxychloroquine; filled both at the discount price, still a stretch. Joints a little better already. Explained steroid side effects to watch for (sleep, appetite, mood, BP). Will see her in 2 weeks to check BP and go over everything in person. Lupus, SLE arthropathy added to list.

documents.title: Follow-up - SLE
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three weeks into prednisone 20 and hydroxychloroquine 200 bid from rheumatology. Knees and wrists much better, morning stiffness down to 20 minutes. Rash fading; wearing a hat at the bus stop. Hungry all the time, sleeping a bit worse. Taking LEV, she thinks better than before since she now has a pill box with the new pills in it too.

Exam: BP 144/92, repeat similar. Wrists with minimal residual puffiness, knees no effusion. Faint malar erythema. Lungs clear, heart regular.

A/P
1. SLE with arthropathy - responding. Continue per rheum. Labs in March for them.
2. Elevated BP on prednisone - recheck in 4 weeks; low-salt advice.
3. Immunosuppressed - PCV20 given today.
4. Epilepsy, asthma - unchanged.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: BP recheck
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BP still up, 146/90 today, and high on the pharmacy kiosk twice last week. On prednisone 20, with lupus. No headache, no chest pain, no swelling. Home salt intake reviewed, eats a lot of takeout on shift.
Assessment: secondary hypertension in setting of steroids and SLE. Starting lisinopril 10 mg daily. BMP with the March labs. Recheck 3 months.

documents.title: Bumps on my face
documents.author: patient
documents.body: For about a week I've had little red bumps on my cheeks and forehead, they're sore when I touch them. Not like the lupus rash. Is this from the prednisone? I have to be at work with customers all day and it's embarrassing.

documents.title: Re: Bumps on my face
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Could well be from the prednisone. I've put in a dermatology referral so they can look and treat it. Also - your rheumatology labs are due, I put the orders in. Can you come by Wednesday morning for the draw?

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CBC now normal. ESR 18, CRP 2.0. Creatinine 0.9, potassium fine on lisinopril. UA clean. Copy faxed to rheumatology and dermatology. Pt notified via portal.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside Dermatology - Consultation
Date of service: 3/22/2022
Allergies: sulfa antibiotics (rash)

27-year-old woman with SLE, on prednisone 20 mg daily since her rheumatology visit in December. Three weeks of a worsening eruption of small, red, tender bumps over the cheeks and forehead. Denies blackheads. Denies deep painful lumps.

Exam: Many uniform small papules across the cheeks and forehead. No open or closed comedones. No cysts or nodules. No scarring. Background malar erythema is faint.

Labs provided by PCP (3/9): CBC normal, ESR 18, CRP 2.0, creatinine 0.9, urinalysis normal.

Assessment: Steroid-induced acne (monomorphic papular eruption).

Plan: Clindamycin 1% gel twice daily. Gentle non-comedogenic cleanser and moisturizer, mineral sunscreen daily. Expect improvement as steroid dose comes down; will defer dosing to rheumatology. Return as needed.

documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside Rheumatology Clinic - Follow-up
Date of service: 4/20/2022

SLE with arthritis, malar rash, cytopenias. On prednisone 20 mg daily and hydroxychloroquine 200 mg bid since December. Joints feel near normal; no morning stiffness beyond a few minutes. Facial rash quiet. Steroid acne being treated by dermatology. BP managed by PCP on lisinopril.

Exam: no synovitis in hands, wrists or knees. Scattered small papules on cheeks. No oral ulcers.

March labs (PCP) reviewed: blood counts recovered, ESR 18, creatinine and urine normal.

Plan: continue current regimen for now. Labs with PCP every 3 months. Follow up in 6 months, sooner if symptoms return.

Regional Emergency Department - Physician Record
Date of service: 12/15/2022
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics (rash)

CC: legs swollen, urine foamy.

HPI: 28F with SLE diagnosed about a year ago, then steroid acne. Several days of swelling in both legs and frothy urine, new tiredness, mild joint aches. Says she stopped all her lupus and blood pressure pills around six months ago because she could not afford them. Still taking her seizure medicine most days and her inhalers.

Exam: BP 148/92. Pitting edema both lower legs. Lungs clear. No rash on face beyond faint papules.

Results: creatinine 2.1. Urine 4+ protein, dysmorphic red cells and red cell casts. Complement C3 and C4 low. Anti-dsDNA elevated.

Impression: Active lupus nephritis.

Disposition: Discussed with on-call nephrology. Restart prednisone 20 mg daily. Outpatient renal biopsy being arranged to determine class. Follow up with PCP within the week. Return for decreased urine, shortness of breath or worsening swelling.

conditions.label: Patient's intentional underdosing of medication regimen due to financial hardship

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Post-ED visit - lupus nephritis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First time I've seen her since May. ED record from 12/15 reviewed.

S: Stopped prednisone, hydroxychloroquine and lisinopril in June when the money ran out; didn't want to tell us. Kept LEV, misses some. Legs started swelling early this month, urine bubbly. Restarted prednisone 20 from the ED Friday. Face bumps gone since summer. Joints a little achy.

O: BP elevated. 2+ pitting edema to mid-shin bilaterally. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Skin: no acne, no malar rash.

Data: Cr 2.1, 4+ protein, dysmorphic RBC and casts, low C3/C4, dsDNA up.

A/P
1. Lupus nephritis, new - biopsy is being set up for 12/29. Restart lisinopril 10 for BP and protein. Nephrology referral placed today. Strict return precautions.
2. Medication underdosing due to cost - long talk, no judgment. Connected with our care coordinator for hospital free-care application and manufacturer programs. Asked her to text me before she ever stops a pill again.
3. Steroid acne - resolved.
4. HTN - restart lisinopril as above.
5. Flu shot today.
See her again right after nephrology.

reports.text: Specimen: kidney, left, percutaneous core biopsy (2 cores). Light microscopy, immunofluorescence and electron microscopy performed. Findings consistent with diffuse proliferative lupus nephritis with immune-complex deposits.

Ultrasound-guided percutaneous left renal biopsy, two cores. No immediate complications. Post-procedure observation 6 hours, hemoglobin stable, discharged home. Pathology to follow; clinic visit 1/5.

documents.title: Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside Nephrology - Consultation
Date of service: 1/5/2023
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics

28-year-old with SLE, presenting in December with nephrotic-range proteinuria, active sediment and creatinine 2.1 after six months off therapy. Biopsy 12/29: class IV lupus nephritis.

Meds: prednisone 20 mg daily (restarted 12/15), lisinopril 10 mg daily (restarted 12/20), levetiracetam 500 mg bid, inhalers. Hydroxychloroquine not resumed - cost.

Exam: edema improving, 1+ at ankles.

Urine pregnancy test negative today. Amenorrheic; counseled that mycophenolate must not be taken in pregnancy.

Assessment: Class IV lupus nephritis.

Plan:
- Mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg twice daily; manufacturer assistance application started in clinic today.
- Continue prednisone 20 mg daily and lisinopril 10 mg.
- CBC, CMP, urinalysis every 4-6 weeks via PCP to start.
- Return 3 months.

documents.title: Mycophenolate assistance
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Care coordinator heard from the manufacturer program: approved for 12 months, first shipment to her home this week. Pt had a starter supply from nephrology and has not missed any doses. Free-care application also submitted for hospital-based labs.

Exam: BP better. Trace ankle edema. Lungs clear.
A/P: lupus nephritis improving clinically. Labs today and forwarded to nephrology. Epilepsy - no events. Asthma fine. RTC 4 months, labs between per nephrology.

Exam: no synovitis. Skin clear.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional Emergency Department - Physician Record
Date of service: 8/29/2023
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics

CC: seizure, not waking up.

HPI: 29-year-old woman with epilepsy and SLE (lupus nephritis on mycophenolate and prednisone). Husband describes a generalized shaking seizure at home lasting about seven minutes; she has not come back to her normal self since. He says she takes her seizure medicine on and off.

Exam on arrival: BP 145/90, HR 110, RR 22, SpO2 96% on room air. Drowsy, withdraws and groans to pain, GCS 10. No tongue laceration noted. No focal limb weakness evident.

IV access obtained, labs sent: Na 140, K 4.2, Cl 102, HCO3 24, glucose 98, creatinine 0.9.

Course: Lorazepam IV and levetiracetam IV load given. No further convulsions. Held overnight in the ED observation unit; GCS 15 by 06:00 and at baseline per husband.

Diagnosis: Generalized tonic-clonic status epilepticus in known epilepsy; missed doses.

Disposition: Discharged home 8/30 on levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily. No driving per state rules. Neurology follow-up; PCP within 1 week.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED visit - status epilepticus
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED record from 8/29 reviewed. Seven-minute generalized seizure, slow to wake, treated and observed overnight; fine by morning.

She is back to normal, sore muscles for two days. Admits she'd missed a few days of LEV that week, ran out and waited for payday. Husband was with her today. He is going to keep the refill dates on his phone too.

Exam: alert, oriented, speech normal. Strength and gait normal. BP fine.

A/P
1. Status epilepticus, resolved; epilepsy on LEV 500 BID. Pharmacy set to auto-refill; told her to text us when she is down to a week of pills. No driving for six months from 8/29 - she takes the bus to work. Referral back to neurology - it has been years.
2. Lupus nephritis - creatinine 0.9 in the ED, nice. Nephrology visit next month.
3. Asthma - fine.

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside Neurology - Consultation
Date of service: 9/27/2023

29-year-old with longstanding generalized epilepsy on levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily, seen after an episode of generalized convulsive status on 8/29 in the setting of missed doses. Also SLE with lupus nephritis on mycophenolate and prednisone.

No events since. No mood side effects from levetiracetam. Neurological exam normal.

Assessment: Generalized epilepsy; breakthrough status attributable to nonadherence rather than failure of the drug.

Plan: Keep levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily; dose is adequate when taken. Adherence plan reviewed with patient and husband (alarms, blister packs, refill synchronization). Seizure first aid reviewed with husband. No driving until 6 months seizure-free. Follow up in 1 year or sooner with any event.

Class IV lupus nephritis, ten months into mycophenolate 1 g bid with prednisone 20 mg and lisinopril 10 mg. Creatinine back to 0.9 (ED, August). Urine protein down to trace, sediment bland. No edema. Brief ED stay in August for a seizure; no renal issue.

Assessment: Complete renal response.

Plan: Continue mycophenolate 1 g twice daily, prednisone 20 mg daily and lisinopril 10 mg. Labs every 3 months with PCP. Return 6 months.

reports.text: Specimen adequate, transformation zone present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.

Regional Emergency Department - Physician Record
Date of service: 4/18/2024
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics

CC: tired, puffy face, dark urine.

HPI: 29F with SLE and class IV lupus nephritis (2022), on mycophenolate, prednisone 20 and lisinopril. Says this feels like the kidney flare in December 2022. Months of aching in hands and wrists, mouth sores coming and going recently. For about a week her eyelids are swollen on waking and her urine looks darker.

documents.author: PCP

Today: eyelid puffiness better, a little ankle swelling. Mouth sores healing. Hand and wrist aches persist. Says she has been taking the mycophenolate; a shipment came late in March and she may have gone a few days without.

Regional Hospital - Medical ICU Discharge Summary
Admitted 8/18/2024, discharged 8/22/2024
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics

Admitting diagnosis: Refractory status epilepticus.

History: 30-year-old woman with SLE, class IV lupus nephritis (flare April 2024), and epilepsy, with an episode of generalized convulsive status one year ago. Brought by ambulance after recurrent seizures at home. Husband reports she has not been taking her medicines reliably for about a month. Paramedics gave lorazepam 4 mg IV en route; she arrived unresponsive. A second lorazepam dose was given and she was intubated for airway protection. Thirty minutes later her level of consciousness had not improved, without visible convulsive activity.

Exam: T 37.2 C, BP 130/85, pulse 88, RR 16 (ventilated). Postictal; no focal neurological deficit identified. Glucose 98.

Course: IV levetiracetam load and maintenance. Continuous EEG showed no ongoing electrographic seizures. Sedation lifted and extubated on hospital day 2. Mental status back to baseline. Renal function and urine monitored and stable during stay. Home mycophenolate, prednisone and lisinopril resumed.

Discharge medications: levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily; mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg twice daily; prednisone 20 mg daily; lisinopril 10 mg daily; fluticasone inhaler; albuterol as needed.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; neurology clinic. No driving for 6 months.

documents.title: Post-discharge visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Discharge summary 8/18-8/22 reviewed: refractory status, intubated, extubated day 2, EEG without ongoing seizures.

With husband today. Feels back to herself. She is quiet about the month before - work hours went up, she stopped filling the pill box, lost track of all of it. No intent to stop. No low mood on PHQ-2 screen.

Exam: alert, fluent, normal gait and strength. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. Status epilepticus, resolved. LEV 500 BID unchanged per hospital and neurology. Husband fills the pill box Sunday nights; pharmacy blister packs set up today. No driving 6 months.
2. Lupus nephritis - recheck labs at nephrology in October.
3. HTN, asthma - stable.
RTC 6-8 weeks, sooner anything.

reports.text: CT angiography of the chest, abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast. Dissection flap begins just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery and extends through the descending thoracic aorta. Ascending aorta and arch not involved. reports.conclusion: Acute type B aortic dissection of the descending thoracic aorta, without malperfusion or rupture.

Regional Trauma Center - Emergency Physician Record

31-year-old woman, restrained driver, head-on collision. History of SLE with lupus nephritis, two episodes of status epilepticus and a type B aortic dissection (2/2025).

Arrival: agitated but alert, GCS 14. BP 130/85, HR 92, RR 22, SpO2 98% room air. Repeat BP 155/90, HR 88, RR 18.

Survey: forehead contusion; no other obvious injury. Pupils equal and reactive, right slightly sluggish. FAST negative.

About two hours after arrival, increasingly drowsy and complaining of right-sided headache. Non-contrast head CT: small right subdural hematoma without significant midline shift. Trauma CT body: no acute injury; known dissection unchanged.

Neurosurgery at bedside; admitted to neuro ICU.

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
Regional Trauma Center - Neurosurgery Operative Report
Date of surgery: 12/29/2025

Preoperative diagnosis: acute right subdural hematoma with midline shift and early uncal herniation.
Procedure: emergency right frontotemporoparietal craniotomy and evacuation of subdural hematoma.

Indication: further decline in level of consciousness; repeat CT with enlargement, 8 mm shift and early uncal herniation.

Findings: acute subdural clot over the right convexity, evacuated. Bone flap replaced. Subdural drain placed.

EBL modest. No complications. To neuro ICU intubated.

Regional Trauma Center - Neurosurgery Discharge Summary
Admitted 12/29/2025, discharged 1/9/2026

Diagnoses: traumatic acute right subdural hematoma with brain herniation, status post right craniotomy and evacuation 12/29/2025. Forehead contusion.

Course: emergency evacuation the night of admission. Extubated postoperative day 1. Drain removed day 2. Postop CT satisfactory. Levetiracetam continued at home dose without seizures. Blood pressure held within dissection goals on home metoprolol and lisinopril. Prednisone and mycophenolate continued. Mental status returned to baseline; no focal deficits. Worked with PT/OT, cleared for home with husband.

Discharge medications: unchanged from admission (levetiracetam 500 mg bid; metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily; lisinopril 10 mg daily; mycophenolate 1000 mg bid; prednisone 20 mg daily; fluticasone; albuterol prn).

Follow-up: neurosurgery 4-6 weeks with CT head. PCP 1 week. Staples out at PCP day 10-14. No driving until cleared by neurosurgery and neurology.

Husband drove her in. Tired, mild incisional soreness, no worsening headache, no vomiting, no weakness, no seizures. Sleeping a lot. Taking every medicine on time - he has the blister packs.

Exam: alert, oriented x3, speech fluent. Pupils equal and reactive. Strength symmetric, gait steady. Right scalp incision clean and dry, staples removed today without difficulty. Forehead bruise fading. Lungs clear. BP within goal.

A/P
1. Traumatic right SDH with herniation, s/p craniotomy - recovering well. Neurosurgery visit with CT on 2/11. No driving. Off work until neurosurgery clears; work note given.
2. Type B dissection - BP controlled; CTA due February.
3. Epilepsy - LEV 500 BID, no events.
4. Lupus nephritis - labs at nephrology in March.
Return precautions for headache, confusion, weakness, seizure.

reports.text: Compared with 12/31/2025. Postoperative change of right craniotomy. No residual or recurrent subdural collection. No midline shift. Ventricles and cisterns normal.
